title: Finding roots: bisection, false position, Newton, secant
subtitle: Most equations cannot be solved with algebra. Numerical methods creep up on the answer instead — and they differ enormously in how fast.

why.title: The problem and the errors
why.body: Solve f(x) = 0 when no formula exists (x³ − x − 2 = 0, cos x = x). Start by locating a root: if f is continuous and f(a), f(b) have opposite signs, a root lies between (intermediate value theorem). Then refine by iteration. Two errors matter: the truncation error of the method and the round-off error of the machine; accuracy is often stated as the tolerance at which iteration stops.
why.steps: f(x) = x³ − x − 2. Test f(1) and f(2). Opposite signs, so a root lies in [1, 2].

bis.title: Bisection
bis.body: Take the midpoint c; keep the half whose ends still have opposite signs. Each step halves the interval: after n steps the error is ≤ (b − a)/2ⁿ. Guaranteed to converge, but slowly (one binary digit per step). For x³ − x − 2 on [1, 2] it reaches 1.5214 in 21 iterations to tolerance 10⁻⁶.
bis.steps: Iterations needed to get within 10⁻⁶ from an interval of length 1. n > log₂(10⁶) ≈ 19.9, so 20 iterations.

falsi.title: False position (regula falsi)
falsi.body: Instead of the midpoint, draw the chord between (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)) and take where it crosses the axis: c = (a·f(b) − b·f(a)) / (f(b) − f(a)). Keep the sub-interval with the sign change, as in bisection. It uses the size of f, so it is usually faster (13 iterations here), though one end can stay stuck for a convex function.

newton.title: Newton–Raphson
newton.body: From a guess xₙ, draw the tangent to f and let it hit the axis: xn+1 = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ). Near a simple root convergence is quadratic — the number of correct digits roughly doubles each step. It needs f′, a good start, and fails where f′ ≈ 0. Finding √2 from x₀ = 1 via f = x² − 2 takes 5 iterations to 10⁻⁹; x³ − x − 2 from 1.5 takes 3.

secant.title: Secant method
secant.body: Replace f′ by the slope through the last two points: xn+1 = xₙ − f(xₙ)(xₙ − xn−1)/(f(xₙ) − f(xn−1)). No derivative needed and no bracket; order of convergence ≈ 1.618. Here 7 iterations. Compare the four methods below on the same equation: root ≈ 1.5214.
